headline: Two-lot subdivision on Worthley Road approved with conditions after neighbors raised driveway and drainage concerns
summary: The plan is for a two-lot subdivision of land for the Knottensun Irrevocable Trust, with the new lot at 22.5 Worthley. Neighbors raised concerns about drainage, the steep driveway, and access to a shared easement, so the approval requires a swale and runoff plan reviewed by the town engineer within six months. The board also approved a two-lot subdivision at 190 Hampstead Road and heard a Southern New Hampshire Planning Commission report on housing readiness in Derry. Earlier, it approved a $58,811 cash escrow for 57 Crystal Avenue and a release of a letter of credit for 35 Maple Street.
decisions: Approved a $58,811 cash escrow for 57 Crystal Avenue, unanimously.
Approved release number two on letter of credit 24284 and a replacement letter of credit of $30,721.68 for 35 Maple Street, unanimously.
Granted a waiver to set lot size by lot area instead of soil size, 7-2.
Granted a waiver so lot lines need not meet streets at substantially right angles, unanimously.
Granted a waiver from the sight distance profile for the new driveway, unanimously.
Granted a waiver to skip granite bounds where existing bounds cannot be removed by statute, unanimously.
Adopted findings that vehicle access and erosion control are adequate, 7-2.
Conditionally approved the two-lot subdivision on Worthley Road, 6-2.
Motion that the 190 Hampstead Road subdivision is a development of regional impact failed, unanimously.
Conditionally approved the two-lot subdivision at 190 Hampstead Road, unanimously.
discussion: Worthley driveway grade and runoff: Neighbors and members discussed the 15% driveway grade and the steep side cuts. The engineer said a swale and rip-rap would divert water, and the approval requires cross-section and runoff plans.

Access during construction: Neighbors asked that the access easement stay open during construction. Members said the easement is private and they lack authority to set work hours, so they noted the issue would be raised when a driveway permit is filed.
Soils and lot size: Members debated whether soil tests should set lot size on the three-acre lot, given ledge concerns. Members said a test pit and state subdivision approval supported the waiver.

Fire truck access: Members raised concerns that long fire engines could not climb the transition from the flat section to the steep grade. The fire marshal reviews driveways, and a note on fire protection was added to the plan.

Hampstead Road drainage: Neighbors of Drew Woods raised concerns that new roof and pavement would add runoff to their backyards. The engineer said the driveway culvert would only carry existing flow and that no drainage facilities are required.
